escalation: Class 11 wrong-link-target, two anchors: both bare "Ib." displays resolve to Yoma 2a (data-ref "Yoma 2a:3" and "Yoma 2a") although every citation they continue is Yerushalmi — the first follows "Y. Sabb. V, beg. 7ᵇ", the second follows "Y. Kil. l. c.; Y. Sabb. l. c.". The correct targets are the Yerushalmi loci the "Ib." abbreviates; the entry contains no bytes spelling them, so no replace is possible. Member of catalogued pattern ib-yoma-2a (312 corpus-wide).

Two findings. (1) Class 11 wrong-link-target, accepting the abbrev-mislink hint: the anchor display הל׳ in "Nidd. 31ᵃ, a. e. הל׳ the white substance (semen virile)" is the definite article plus a geresh abbreviation of this entry's own headword לוֹבֶן, but data-ref names חֶלמוֹן (H01091), whose own gloss is "yolk, yellow of an egg" — the opposite substance. The resolution path is H01091's alt_headwords item "(הֶל׳)", not the headword. Correct target is this entry. (2) Sense 1)'s definition ends with a stranded em-dash and the following sibling's number is "*2)": print reads "—*2)", so the em-dash is the next marker's separator left behind on the previous sense. retag cannot express "—*2)" (outside the closed marker grammar) and delete would drop a byte print has.

Class 11 wrong-link-target. The lead sense reads " (or לַגָּא) ch. same, "; the anchor display לַגָּא is an alternative spelling of THIS entry's headword לוּגָּא (alt_headwords already carries לֻגָּא), but data-ref names לֹג — the Hebrew entry L00183 of which this entry is declared the Chaldaic cognate. The skeletons differ (לגא vs לג), so no documented display-vs-target carve-out applies, and a headword לגא does exist (L00121). Correct target is this entry or none; the entry has no bytes to replace the data-ref with. (The unnumbered "ch. same," preamble before 1) is the documented preamble shape, not implied-one — no retag proposed.)

Class 8 lost-parenthetical. The definition ends "; (Lev. R. s. 20 שמצה, Ar. .": the parenthesis opened before "Lev. R. s. 20" never closes (entry-level count 2 "(" vs 1 ")"), and the trailing "Ar. ." is a truncated Ar. variant citation — the variant reading and the closing paren were lost upstream, leaving an orphan period. Restoration needs bytes not present in the entry.

Array-scope defect outside patch scope: alt_headwords[1] is "(לוּדָאָה)" — the print parentheses were captured into the value, so the variant is unusable as a lookup key (catalogued pattern parenthesized-alt-headword, 580 corpus-wide). No sense-scope op can write alt_headwords. Judged and NOT escalated: the anchor display לידה (Ms. O. variant of the Amora's name) resolving to לֵידָה "birth" is within the v4 niqqud carve-out — exactly one corpus headword carries the skeleton לידה — although the target is semantically unrelated.

Class 11 wrong-link-target, accepting the one-consonant-diverge hint. In sense —2) the text reads "(not הוה; prob. to be read: לוּדָיִין)" — an emendation Jastrow proposes AGAINST the transmitted ללוּדָנִין of the same line. The anchor on the emendation targets לוּדָנִין (L00203), the very reading it corrects, differing by one interior consonant (י for נ); לוּדָיִין is no corpus headword. L00203's entire content is ", Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᵈ top, v. לוּדָאָה 2", i.e. a stub pointing back at this sense, so the link is a no-op loop asserting an identity the text denies. Maintainer call whether the emendation should be unlinked or linked here.

Class 11 wrong-link-target. The entry opens ", pl. לוֹדִים" — the plural of this headword לוֹדִי — but the anchor's data-ref names לוּדִים (L00199, "keepers of gladiators"), a different lemma distinguished from this one by vocalization alone. The entry itself supplies the witness: two clauses later it writes "—[V. לוּדִים.]" as a separate see-reference to that same target, so by the entry's own testimony לוֹדִים and לוּדִים are not the same word. Two headwords share the skeleton לודים, so the v4 niqqud carve-out cannot apply. Correct target is this entry.

Class 8 lost-parenthetical. Sense —2) has 2 "(" against 3 ")": the run "; Tanḥ. ib. 14 בבלורית בקסמים ובזנות)." closes a parenthesis that was never opened — print brackets the parallel Tanḥuma citation, and its opening "(" is missing before "Tanḥ. ib. 14". Repairing needs a byte the entry does not contain; deleting the surviving ")" instead would drop a byte print has.
